Akshaye Khanna is honestly one of the most underrated actors we have. The kind of calm intensity he brings is rare  he doesn’t need loud acting, his expressions and screen presence alone create impact. He has already proven how versatile he is, from serious roles to negative characters to full-on emotional performances.
If Dhurandhar gives him a properly written character, trust me he will own that role. Akshaye Khanna is the kind of actor who can turn even an average scene into something memorable. With strong writing, he won’t just perform well  he’ll completely steal the show

So that's it. 
Hope I'll get my answer

snippet.textDisplay:
I can't believe six months back when I first saw this trailer, I was just mildly impressed. Not interested enough to actually watch this movie since I had very very VERY low expectations of Hindi movie industry. I dismissed the trailer as exaggerated parts of the movie just to arouse interest.

Cut to today. 

Oh man! What a change! I have watched this and its sequel several times already and can't get enough of it. I judge every movie, past or future, in comparison with Dhurandhar and none ever matches upto the standard that Dhurandhar has set.

snippet.textDisplay: Aditya Dhar is playing 4D chess with our minds! Looking back at this trailer after watching Part 1, it’s absolute genius how he fooled everyone. He packed almost the entire Part 1 trailer with footage from Dhurandhar: The Revenge. We spent the whole first movie waiting for these specific scenes, completely unaware that he was already building the bridge to the 2026 sequel. It kept Part 1 entirely spoiler-free while seamlessly setting up the universe. Absolute masterclass in direction and marketing.

snippet.textDisplay:
वही पुरानी घिसी-पिटी कहानी! बिना पाकिस्तान का नाम लिए ये लोग कोई फिल्म बना ही नहीं सकते। इससे बेहतर तो साउथ की फिल्में हैं, इसीलिए तो वो आज सबसे आगे हैं।"


​१. ओरिजिनल और अनोखी कहानियाँ 

​साउथ के डायरेक्टर्स बिल्कुल नई और ज़मीन से जुड़ी कहानियों पर काम करते हैं। वो अपनी लोक-कथाओं (folklore), पौराणिक कहानियों और पारिवारिक भावनाओं को इस तरह पर्दे पर लाते हैं जो दर्शकों ने पहले कभी नहीं देखा। 'कांतारा' (Kantara), 'बाहुबली' (Baahubali) या 'पुष्पा' (Pushpa) जैसी फिल्मों को चलने के लिए किसी भारत-पाकिस्तान के फॉर्मूले की ज़रूरत नहीं पड़ी, फिर भी इन्होंने दुनिया भर में तहलका मचा दिया।

​२. अपनी संस्कृति और जड़ों से जुड़ाव 

​साउथ की फिल्में अपनी संस्कृति और परंपराओं को बहुत गर्व के साथ पर्दे पर दिखाती हैं। वो हॉलीवुड या किसी विदेशी स्टाइल की नकल नहीं करते। इसी 'देसी फील' की वजह से आम दर्शक उनकी फिल्मों से बहुत आसानी से जुड़ जाते हैं।

​३. दर्शकों के मनोरंजन को प्राथमिकता 

​आजकल बॉलीवुड की कई बड़ी फिल्में एक खास पॉलिटिकल फॉर्मूले या प्रोपेगैंडा के तहत बनती हैं, जिससे कहानी की गहराई खत्म हो जाती है। इसके विपरीत, साउथ की फिल्मों का मुख्य मकसद शुद्ध मनोरंजन (Pure Entertainment) और बेहतरीन विज़ुअल्स के ज़रिए दर्शकों का दिल जीतना होता है। वो एक्शन और इमोशन का ऐसा तालमेल बनाते हैं जो पैसा वसूल करा देता है।

​४. स्टार्स से बड़ी कहानी 

​साउथ इंडस्ट्री में कहानी को 'हीरो' बनाया जाता है। वहाँ कोई कितना भी बड़ा सुपरस्टार क्यों न हो, अगर फिल्म की स्क्रिप्ट कमज़ोर है, तो दर्शक उसे नकार देते हैं। इसी डर की वजह से वहाँ के मेकर्स कहानी लिखने में कड़ी मेहनत करते हैं, जो आजकल बॉलीवुड में बहुत कम देखने को मिलता है।

​निष्कर्ष 

अगर बॉलीवुड इस पुराने और उबाऊ फॉर्मूले से बाहर नहीं निकला, तो वो और पीछे छूट जाएगा। इसमें कोई शक नहीं है कि साउथ की फिल्में अपनी बेहतरीन कहानियों और मेकिंग के दम पर ही आज पूरे सिनेमा जगत पर राज कर रही हैं।
snippet.textOriginal:
वही पुरानी घिसी-पिटी कहानी! बिना पाकिस्तान का नाम लिए ये लोग कोई फिल्म बना ही नहीं सकते। इससे बेहतर तो साउथ की फिल्में हैं, इसीलिए तो वो आज सबसे आगे हैं।"


​१. ओरिजिनल और अनोखी कहानियाँ 

​साउथ के डायरेक्टर्स बिल्कुल नई और ज़मीन से जुड़ी कहानियों पर काम करते हैं। वो अपनी लोक-कथाओं (folklore), पौराणिक कहानियों और पारिवारिक भावनाओं को इस तरह पर्दे पर लाते हैं जो दर्शकों ने पहले कभी नहीं देखा। 'कांतारा' (Kantara), 'बाहुबली' (Baahubali) या 'पुष्पा' (Pushpa) जैसी फिल्मों को चलने के लिए किसी भारत-पाकिस्तान के फॉर्मूले की ज़रूरत नहीं पड़ी, फिर भी इन्होंने दुनिया भर में तहलका मचा दिया।

​२. अपनी संस्कृति और जड़ों से जुड़ाव 

​साउथ की फिल्में अपनी संस्कृति और परंपराओं को बहुत गर्व के साथ पर्दे पर दिखाती हैं। वो हॉलीवुड या किसी विदेशी स्टाइल की नकल नहीं करते। इसी 'देसी फील' की वजह से आम दर्शक उनकी फिल्मों से बहुत आसानी से जुड़ जाते हैं।

​३. दर्शकों के मनोरंजन को प्राथमिकता 

​आजकल बॉलीवुड की कई बड़ी फिल्में एक खास पॉलिटिकल फॉर्मूले या प्रोपेगैंडा के तहत बनती हैं, जिससे कहानी की गहराई खत्म हो जाती है। इसके विपरीत, साउथ की फिल्मों का मुख्य मकसद शुद्ध मनोरंजन (Pure Entertainment) और बेहतरीन विज़ुअल्स के ज़रिए दर्शकों का दिल जीतना होता है। वो एक्शन और इमोशन का ऐसा तालमेल बनाते हैं जो पैसा वसूल करा देता है।

​४. स्टार्स से बड़ी कहानी 

​साउथ इंडस्ट्री में कहानी को 'हीरो' बनाया जाता है। वहाँ कोई कितना भी बड़ा सुपरस्टार क्यों न हो, अगर फिल्म की स्क्रिप्ट कमज़ोर है, तो दर्शक उसे नकार देते हैं। इसी डर की वजह से वहाँ के मेकर्स कहानी लिखने में कड़ी मेहनत करते हैं, जो आजकल बॉलीवुड में बहुत कम देखने को मिलता है।

अगर बॉलीवुड इस पुराने और उबाऊ फॉर्मूले से बाहर नहीं निकला, तो वो और पीछे छूट जाएगा। इसमें कोई शक नहीं है कि साउथ की फिल्में अपनी बेहतरीन कहानियों और मेकिंग के दम पर ही आज पूरे सिनेमा जगत पर राज कर रही हैं।

snippet.textDisplay:
Technical Analysis: Production Oversight in Durandharam
Subject: Continuity and Physical Realism Errors in the Climax Sequence
Observer Perspective: Professional Telugu Art Director
The Sequence Breakdown
In the climax of the movie Durandharam, the protagonist carries a cache of guns into a structure resembling a mosque. When the antagonists attempt to open the weapon crates, a concealed bomb detonates.
The Scale of the Explosion
The impact of the blast is depicted as massive. The entire building shakes violently, and the explosion—occurring in the underground section—is powerful enough to shatter and collapse an entire concrete slab.
The Technical Oversight (The Flaw)
Despite the sheer magnitude of the blast that caused structural failure (the collapsing slab), there is a glaring lack of environmental reaction:
Window Integrity: Not a single glass pane in the building’s windows shatters or even cracks.
Chandeliers & Lighting: The large, ornate chandeliers hanging in the hall, which are made of delicate glass components, remain perfectly intact. They don't break, fall, or lose a single crystal.
Professional Conclusion
As a Telugu Art Director, I am pointing this out as a significant lapse in coordination between the Production Designer, Director, and Cinematographer.
When a blast is powerful enough to bring down a ceiling slab, the resulting shockwave would realistically pulverize every glass surface in the vicinity. This lack of "destruction detail" creates a disconnect in the visual storytelling and undermines the stakes of the scene.

snippet.textDisplay: Dhurandhar tries to show how Indian RAW functions, but honestly it just makes them look stupid. RAW sends Hamza undercover to infiltrate Rahman’s small rebel group and kill him. But to get close, Hamza actually saves Rahman from an assassination attempt, only to later spend so much time trying to kill him himself. That is what makes the whole plan look dumb. Rahman could have died in the first place, but RAW instead risks everything for no reason. So instead of looking smart, the mission just feels unintentionally funny.

snippet.textDisplay:
I just watched this movie and honestly… it was a COMPLETE disaster 🤦🏻‍♀️🤦🏻‍♀️🤦🏻‍♀️ I don’t even know where to start.

First of all, the way they used Islam in the story was absolutely ridiculous. It felt like they just threw in stereotypes and violence without any real understanding. Islam is literally a religion built on peace, compassion, charity, and respect for humanity — but instead they twisted it into something totally unrecognizable. It’s honestly frustrating to see the same tired, inaccurate narratives being recycled again and again.

And then on top of that they dragged Pakistan into it too? 🤦‍♀️ Seriously? Portraying Pakistanis in such a negative, one-dimensional way is just lazy storytelling. There are over a billion Muslims in the world living normal, peaceful lives every single day, but somehow movies like this always choose the same old harmful clichés.

Instead of learning, researching, or representing cultures responsibly, they went for shock value and stereotypes. That’s not bold filmmaking — that’s just bad writing.

For me this movie is a total flop. Not entertaining, not thoughtful, not even remotely accurate. Just disappointing from start to finish.

Islam is not what they showed. It’s a religion of peace, community, and mercy — and it deserves better representation than this. 💯

snippet.textDisplay:
The film is built as this big inspirational spy thriller, meant to hype up Indian intelligence ops, RAW heroism, and the idea that one determined agent can turn the tide against terror networks. But then it deliberately paints the Pakistani side—gangsters, ISI operatives like Arjun Rampal's Major Iqbal (the "Angel of Death" character, inspired by real figures like Ilyas Kashmiri)—as these towering, ripped, unflinching, hyper-masculine figures who exude zero fear of India or its agents.
Rampal's ISI Major is shown training hard (punching bags, that controlled menace), commanding respect in his world, and orchestrating plots with cold efficiency. The gangsters (Akshaye Khanna's Rehman Dakait especially) come across as charismatic, physically imposing underworld kings who aren't cartoon villains but real threats—ruthless, fearless, and in their element. Even side characters feel "in a different league" physically and psychologically intimidating.
How does that motivate anyone in real life to pursue espionage or counter-terror careers? Instead of making the enemy seem beatable (like in some older films where antagonists are portrayed as cowardly or incompetent), the movie amps up their strength and intimidation factor. It creates this vibe of "entering Pakistan means facing hell—tall, bulky, no-fear dudes who punch back harder and breathe down your neck constantly." That doesn't scream "join RAW, it's empowering!" It almost feels like a cautionary tale: "This path is insanely dangerous, the other side is built different, and you'll be outnumbered/outmuscled at every turn."
Critics and audiences have echoed similar discomforts. Some reviews call out the film's "aggressive hyper-masculinity" overall (not just on the Pakistani side—Ranveer's Hamza is also ultra-intense and physical). Others note the portrayal isn't cartoonish caricature but surprisingly "nuanced" in showing Pakistan's underworld as gritty and capable, which makes the heroism feel more grueling than glorious. In Pakistan, reactions ranged from praising the craftsmanship to criticizing inaccuracies or glorification of certain figures, but the intimidation factor you mention seems to hit home for cross-border viewers too.
The intent might be to make the stakes feel real and high (no easy wins, true espionage is brutal), to show respect for the adversary in a twisted "worthy enemy" way, or even to justify the "new India" aggressive response (as the film's tagline hammers: entering homes to finish the job). But yeah, it backfires on the motivational angle—if anything, it could discourage rather than encourage aspiring spies by making the mission look overwhelmingly daunting.

snippet.textDisplay:
Propaganda movies often succeed because they use strong feelings people already have, like anger, fear, pride, or bias. If someone already dislikes a group or country, the movie can support what they believe. Then it feels true even when facts are missing.

But not everyone has hate inside them. Some people are influenced because they hear the same message many times, or because the story is emotional and well-made. These movies can also succeed because of marketing, nationalism, and simple good versus bad storytelling.

A propaganda movie often shows one side as completely good and the other as completely evil. It uses emotion more than proof, and it makes people feel wrong for questioning it.

Dhurendhar is an engaging film that stands out mainly because of its powerful performances. Akshay Khanna delivers a mind-blowing act, bringing depth, intensity, and maturity to his character. Ranveer Singh’s performance is equally awesome — energetic, expressive, and full of charisma that lights up every scene he is in. Sanjay Dutt adds strong screen presence, and his acting is impressive, giving the film weight and authority.

The supporting cast also does a wonderful job; every character feels well-done and contributes to the story. The film maintains good pace and keeps the audience connected throughout. Overall, Dhurendhar shines because of its stellar performances and is definitely worth watching for fans of strong acting. 👍👍

snippet.textDisplay:
Not sure how many who watched Dhurandhar realized this, but we watched the whole movie from Ranveer Singh's / Hamza's perspective. Every emotion he put us through while being so restrained on screen..
Hamza's wants to join Rehman's gang , we root for him 

Hamza acts loyal to Dakait and impresses them and want to enter politics, we root for Rehman against Jameel and Khanani 

Hamza wants to save Rehman from Jinn and we believe it is worth protecting Rehman 

Hamza wants to betray Rehman and gang and we are at the edge of our seats to see how Hamza will pull it off.

Everything happening in Lyari we watch through Hamza's lens 

We are not in awe of him yet but we are hooked 

For those who realized how Ranveer connected us to the character so sneakily and  effortlessly without us knowing nothing about his past or any emotional attachment to his character yet.. 🥂

snippet.textDisplay:
We should also understand the political context of India at the time of the Mumbai terror attacks! The time when Mumbai ATS chief Hemant Karkare discovered that the Samjotha express blast and the Malegaon blast were carried out by Hindutva forces and that an organization called Abhinav Bharat was responsible! The time when Thakur, Colonel Purohit and Swami Aseemanand were arrested as accused! The time when the country recognized saffron terrorism as well as Islamic terrorist groups! That is when the Mumbai terror attacks took place. With this, the entire attention of the country shifted away from this. Hemant Karkare, who was not on duty that night, was called in. Hemant Karkare was killed that fateful night. Although the Mumbai police said that he was killed by Pakistani terrorists from a distance, the postmortem revealed that the bullet that hit his body came from close range. His wife Kavita Karkare also raised doubts about this. But the UPA government that ruled the center at that time did not conduct a proper investigation, in other words, even at that time, Hindutva forces had enough influence in the investigation team! This is indicated in the book Who Killed Karkare by the then l G SM Mushrif.  The mastermind of this blast, David Calman Headly, is still in America. Even European countries have expressed suspicion that he is a CIA agent. Although the suicide bomber Ajmal Kasab was killed, the US did not extradite the mastermind, Headly, to India.

Instead of thrilling the people by releasing propaganda films, we need to find the black hands behind this terror and punish the mastermind, David Headley. The political parties' links with Pakistani terrorists should also be exposed.
